commits.message:
feat(email-parsing): self-learning hotlist vs. job-requirement classification

Adds the correction feedback loop for classify_email_by_confidence()
(app/email_parsing/parsers.py) -- a genuinely ambiguous email (content
alone can't decide) now checks whether the sender's own domain has a
consistent correction history before falling through to a generic
keyword guess. A confidently content-classified email is left
completely alone; this only ever breaks a tie.

New: app/email_parsing/classification_learning.py --
record_classification_correction() writes a row to the
classification_feedback table per sender domain (not full address --
one staffing company's several recruiters should teach each other);
get_domain_bias() returns the favored kind once a domain has more than
one correction on record (a single correction could be a one-off
mistake, not yet a pattern).

New capture point: POST /drafts/{id}/reclassify (app/routers/drafts.py,
app/drafts/service.py: reclassify_draft_object()) lets a reviewer
correct a draft's type in place -- it does not create a second draft
for the same email. When the correction moves between draft_hotlist and
draft_job_requirement (the only two kinds the classifier actually
distinguishes), it also feeds classification_learning -- corrections
into/out of other draft types (resume, vendor list, etc.) still apply
but aren't fed into that loop, since the classifier this teaches never
chooses those. This is the backend capture mechanism the review
frontend (not yet built) will call; useful and testable on its own
before that exists.

Wired into detect_document_kind() (app/channels/service.py): the
domain-bias check sits strictly between the content classifier giving
up (ambiguous) and the generic keyword-marker fallback -- a real
per-sender pattern beats a content-blind keyword list, but never
overrides a confident content-based read.

Verified: 9 new tests (no-op on an agreeing correction, no bias below
the minimum-corrections threshold, bias established and correctly
favored/counted/scored once past it, bias is per-domain not per-
address, malformed/missing sender handled without crashing, reclassify
updates draft_type and feeds the loop only for the two learnable types,
reclassifying an unknown draft returns None rather than raising, and an
end-to-end detect_document_kind call that resolves via domain bias for
genuinely unstructured text). Full existing 9-script regression suite
plus retry/DLQ suite and an app-boot check re-run clean afterward.
